notes: καθ᾿ ὑμᾶς → 'your own': the preposition is compressed into the possessive and is unrepresented under rule 36, which names exactly this case, and the article is emptied under rule 20 because ὑμᾶς is present and unspent to take the possessive.
ὄψεσθε keeps 'look to it' whole with the head on the verb word; the supplied 'it' is a rule 7 object helper on the verb that requires it in English.
αὐτοί is rendered by a single English word, so rule 107's two-word case does not arise and 'yourselves' is the head.
ἐστιν is expressed, so rule 68's supplied-copula configurations do not apply and the supplied subject 'they' rides with the verb under rule 9.
